problem: Zero-shot goal-oriented navigation methods (graph-based such as SG-Nav and UniGoal, map-based such as L3MVN and VLFM) focus on exploring new regions and lack memory of explored areas. Targets that are missed or fail viewpoint-sensitive matching are rarely revisited, which hurts instance-level navigation.
motivation: Graph representations are sensitive to viewpoint changes and drop fine-grained attributes. Dense semantic occupancy maps are too large for an LLM to query directly. The paper argues for a sparse, queryable memory that lets the agent re-assess seen objects and revisit regions where the goal may be hidden.
key_idea: Build a sparse dynamic cognitive map of goal-related and co-occurring objects with their best views, then use a VLM to re-validate seen candidates and re-explore explored regions where the goal is likely hidden, stabilized by a blacklist and a double check.
insight: The blacklist matters most: removing it from the full memory-aware strategy drops IIN SR from 60.1 to 52.1 (Table 3, Exp c vs d), because repeated revisits of false candidates waste steps. Memory re-exploration adds gains stepwise: base 55.8, +CMap/GR/BL 57.4, +MGR 60.1, +DC 61.4. Gains are largest on instance-level tasks, and small on category-level ObjNav (+0.3 SR), where precise instance discrimination is less needed.
method: Base navigation: frontier-based exploration on a Mask R-CNN semantic occupancy map (720x720, 0.05 m), frontier clusters via PCA, nearest frontier chosen every 20 steps, Fast Marching local policy; IIN verification with LightGlue keypoint matching, ON/TN with category matching.

Dynamic cognitive map: detects objects from C_base plus goal-related objects C_LLM inferred by an LLM/VLM, using Grounding-DINO+SAM, point clouds with voxel downsampling and DBSCAN, and IoU-based multi-frame fusion. Objects detected more than 3 times become nodes <category, point cloud, (x,y), ranked full-frame images>, ranked by 0.5*confidence+0.5*area ratio.
Unified goal representation G={c, a_int, a_ext}: category, intrinsic and extrinsic attributes extracted by a VLM from the image (IIN) or text (TN); for ON only the category is used.

Goal re-validation: for map nodes matching the goal category, computes a spatial score (Jaccard overlap of neighbors within radius r with C_LLM) and VLM intrinsic/extrinsic similarity scores on the best image. The mean of the three is the confidence; if it exceeds tau_rev=0.7 the agent returns, does a 360° scan and rematches.

Missed goal re-exploration: for map nodes whose category is in C_LLM, the VLM outputs a likelihood that the goal is nearby but unseen. If it exceeds tau_ree=0.5, the agent goes there and scans 360°; otherwise it uses default frontier exploration.
Blacklist: a node is temporarily blacklisted after 3 consecutive failed re-validations, and permanently blacklisted if it passes from afar but fails verification on arrival.
Double check: for ON, a map consistency check against cognitive-map nodes in the region; for IIN/TN, a VLM compares the current observation with G before committing to a temporary goal.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B (frozen) as LLM/VLM, plus Mask R-CNN, Grounding-DINO, SAM, LightGlue
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (640x480, camera height 0.88 m) plus odometry pose
setting.action_space: low-level move_forward 0.25 m / turn_left / turn_right 30° / stop, with a Fast Marching local planner to long-term goals

numbers_note: Split is given only as the dataset version (HM3Dv1/v2 episode counts) and no official split name is stated, so 'val' is assumed. The IIN benchmark is mapped to HM3D-IIN and TN to TextNav. No real-robot numbers are reported.
results: MCNav reaches 61.4 SR / 23.9 SPL on IIN, above UniGoal (60.2/23.7) and Mod-IIN (56.1/23.3). On TN it reaches 22.9/11.7, above UniGoal (20.2/11.4) and GOAT (17.0/8.8). On ObjNav it reaches 54.8/25.1, a small gain over UniGoal's 54.5, and is below WMNav with Gemini (58.1) but above WMNav with Qwen2.5 (46.1).
limitations: Gain on category-level ObjNav is marginal (+0.3 SR over UniGoal), and it trails WMNav with the Gemini backbone (58.1 SR).
Absolute SPL on IIN and TN remains low (23.9 and 11.7), and TN success is only 22.9.
Performance depends on the VLM (Llava-7B 58.7 vs Qwen2.5-VL-7B 61.4 SR) and on tuned thresholds, and the real-robot evaluation is only qualitative demos with no numbers.
